tier_reason: Upgraded from D: Meta's React Native blog post 'Hermes as the Default' (source in facebook/react-native-website) gives first-party start-up, size and memory numbers for the Mattermost app with Hermes versus stock React Native on JavaScriptCore, on a Samsung Galaxy S20 and an iPhone 12 Pro; no measurement harness, build flags or engine versions are published, so not A, and the publisher is the project owner, so not B. The in-repo blog (doc/blog) adds first-party Octane-style charts against QuickJS whose benchmark code is public (benchmarks/octane, benchmarks/bench-runner) but with no compiler flags and, for the 2025 charts, no hardware.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Mattermost app start-up (time from pressing the app icon to the first screen rendered), Hermes vs stock React Native on JavaScriptCore: Android (Samsung Galaxy S20) 1.97 s vs 0.96 s, '51% faster' (about 2.05x, derived from page data); iOS (iPhone 12 Pro) 0.52 s vs 0.19 s, '63% faster' (about 2.7x, derived from page data). Same page: raw APK (arm64-v8a) 72.1 MB vs 58.2 MB, IPA 23.2 MB vs 27.6 MB (+4.4 MB, larger with Hermes), memory 398 MB vs 305 MB (Android) and 120 MB vs 107 MB (iOS). Throughput (repo doc/blog/2025-07-15, bar charts relative to QuickJS = 1.0, values read off the chart): stable Hermes interpreter about 0.96x-2.0x QuickJS across Octane plus three React benchmarks (zlib slightly slower); static_h 'Hermes v2' interpreter about 1.6x-4.6x and with JIT about 2.0x-5.6x.
corrections.baseline: JavaScriptCore as shipped in stock React Native (start-up, memory, binary size); QuickJS for the throughput charts in the repo's own blog. V8, the listed baseline, is not compared on any page opened (Kudo/react-native-js-benchmark compares JSC, V8 and Hermes, but its results are in Google Sheets that are blocked here).
corrections.workload: Mattermost React Native app: cold start-up (app icon press to first screen rendered), memory over a couple of minutes of identical use, and APK/IPA size, on Android and iOS; separately Octane benchmarks plus custom React benchmarks (benchmarks/ in the repo) relative to QuickJS.
corrections.hardware: Samsung Galaxy S20 (Android) and iPhone 12 Pro (iOS) for the start-up numbers; Raspberry Pi 3 and Raspberry Pi 5 for the 2024 Octane charts; the 2025 QuickJS-relative charts state no hardware.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 11.3k stars, 874 forks; default JavaScript engine of React Native since 0.70
corrections.caveats: Start-up, memory and size numbers are first-party (Meta's React Native blog, 2022) on one app (Mattermost) with no published harness, build flags or engine versions; the 'faster' percentages are time reductions (51% and 63%), not speedup factors. The win comes mostly from shipping precompiled bytecode instead of parsing source at start-up; Hermes has no JIT in stable releases, and the JavaScriptCore it replaced in React Native runs with limited JIT (Kudo/react-native-js-benchmark notes React Native Android does not enable all JSC JIT tiers), so this is not a throughput claim against a full JIT engine. IPA size grows by 4.4 MB on iOS. Callstack's independent iOS measurement (about 40% faster start-up and about 18% less memory than JSC for Mattermost, 2.4 MiB size overhead) is seen only as quoted in reactnative.dev's 2021 post 'Toward Hermes being the Default' and in a search snippet; callstack.com is blocked here. Throughput charts against QuickJS are first-party bar charts without exact values or compiler flags; stable Hermes is about level with QuickJS on zlib. Other in-repo figures (JSON.parse 2.7x-3.4x faster, Hades GC 34x shorter p99.9 pauses, static_h 1.1x-7.9x on Octane) compare Hermes with older Hermes, not with a baseline.

notes: The original benchmark_url (repo front page) has no numbers and no baseline comparison (the two false flags refer to it); the corrected benchmark_url was read from its source file in facebook/react-native-website, including the two result images. Metadata checked on github.com: MIT, 11.3k stars, not archived, default branch static_h, last commit 2026-10-05, so active and copyable. Shortcomings to record: first-party single-app start-up numbers without harness or flags, baseline is JavaScriptCore not the listed V8, iOS binary grows 4.4 MB, QuickJS throughput charts are approximate and stable Hermes is not faster on zlib.
